To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and earth; He gives daughters or sons or both to whom He wills, and makes whom He wills barren.
Allah speaks to a human only by revelation, from behind a partition or through a messenger; so He revealed to the Prophet a light that guides to Allah's straight path.
By the clear Book, Allah made it an Arabic Quran to be understood, exalted in the Mother of the Book, and will not turn the message away from transgressors.
Every prophet sent to former peoples was ridiculed, and Allah destroyed peoples greater in power than these.
They admit the Exalted, the Knowing created the heavens and earth; He made the earth a bed, sends rain, and gave ships and animals to ride, exalting Him when mounted.
They assign Allah daughters, leaving sons for themselves, grieve at such news, call the angels females, and claim Allah willed their worship, without knowledge.
They follow their fathers' religion without any book, as every city's affluent told its warners; offered better guidance they still disbelieved, and Allah took retribution on them.
Abraham disassociated himself from what his father and people worshipped, except his Creator who will guide him, and left this word among his descendants.
When truth and a clear Messenger came, they called it magic and asked why the Quran was not sent to a great man; Allah apportions livelihood, His mercy being better.
Were it not that people would become one community, Allah would give disbelievers houses of silver and gold, yet that is worldly enjoyment, and the Hereafter is for the righteous.
Whoever is blinded from the remembrance of the Most Merciful is given a devil companion who averts him while he thinks himself guided, until he regrets it on the Day.
The Prophet cannot make the deaf hear; Allah will take retribution whether or not he sees it, so he holds to the revelation, a reminder for him and his people.
The earlier messengers can be asked whether Allah ever made deities to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful.
Moses brought signs to Pharaoh and his establishment, who laughed and broke their word when affliction lifted; Pharaoh boasted of his kingdom and belittled Moses, and his people were drowned.
When the son of Mary was given as an example, people laughed; Jesus was a favored servant who brought clear proofs and told them to worship Allah, but sects differed.
They await only the Hour coming suddenly, when close friends will become enemies to each other except the righteous.
Allah's servants who believed in His verses and were Muslims enter Paradise without fear or grief, with gold vessels, whatever souls desire and much fruit, forever, for what they did.
The criminals abide in Hell's punishment in despair, calling on Malik to end them, but are told they will remain, having been averse to the truth.
If they devise a plan, Allah also devises; He hears their secrets and private talk, and His messengers with them are recording.
The Lord of the heavens and earth is above having a son; He alone is deity in heaven and earth, knows the Hour, and those invoked besides Him cannot intercede.
The Prophet's saying that these people do not believe is acknowledged; he is told to turn aside from them and say 'Peace', for they will come to know.
By the clear Book, Allah sent it down to warn on a blessed night, the Night of Decree, when every precise matter is made distinct, as mercy from your Lord.
He is Lord of the heavens and earth; there is no deity but Him, who gives life and death, Lord of you and of your first forefathers.
Doubters are to watch for the Day the sky brings visible smoke covering people; they will plead belief despite rejecting a clear Messenger, and once relieved will return.
Pharaoh's people were tried when Moses, a noble messenger, asked for Allah's servants; he left by night with them, and the army drowned, leaving gardens and springs to another people.
Allah saved the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's humiliating torment, chose them knowingly over the worlds, and gave them signs containing a clear trial.
These people say there is only the first death and no resurrection, demanding their forefathers back; yet the people of Tubba' and those before them were destroyed as criminals.
Allah did not create the heavens, the earth and what is between them in play, but in truth, though most do not know.
The Day of Judgement is the appointed time for all, when no relative can help another, except those on whom Allah has mercy.
The tree of zaqqum is food for the sinful, boiling in their bellies; the sinner is dragged into Hellfire, scalding water poured on his head, and mocked as 'the honored'.
The righteous are secure among gardens and springs, in silk, married to fair women with large eyes, with every fruit, tasting no death but the first, protected from Hellfire.
The Quran is made easy in the Prophet's tongue so they may be reminded; so watch, for they are watching.
The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
The heavens and earth, people and creatures, night and day, provision sent from the sky to revive the earth, and the winds are signs for those who believe and reason.
Woe to every sinful liar who hears Allah's verses yet persists arrogantly or takes them in ridicule; Hell is before him, while this Quran is guidance.
Allah subjected the sea for ships and all in the heavens and earth to people, signs for those who give thought.
Believers are told to forgive those who do not expect Allah's days, for He will recompense each people; good and evil deeds count for or against the doer.
Allah gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, judgement and prophethood, provision and preference, but they differed after knowledge out of jealousy, and He will judge between them.
The Prophet must follow an ordained way, not the desires of those who do not know; wrongdoers ally together, Allah protects the righteous, and this Quran is guidance.
Evildoers will not be made equal to righteous believers in life and death; Allah created the heavens and earth in truth so every soul is recompensed without wrong.
